newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy move on reserve rule seen as technical.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy move on reserve rule seen as technical.

text.p: The Bank of Italy's decision to raise the portion of the minimum reserve requirement that banks are allowed to invest on the interbank market was said by analysts to be a technical move to increase liquidity.
"The aim of this move was to give more liquidity to the system," said Giuliano Gasparini at Bologna-based economic research institute Prometeia.
The official minimum reserve requirement -- the percentage of deposits that depositary institutions must set aside with the central bank -- is unchanged at 15 percent.
But the central bank raised to 12.5 percent from 10 percent the portion of the reserve requirement that banks can mobilise on the interbank market.
The move would raise the amount that banks can invest on the market to 8.36 trillion lire from 6.69 trillion lire.

"The Bank of Italy in this way gives more confidence to the market. The handling of the reserve requirement and therefore of liquidity can be managed better," said Alberto Varisco, President of the Italian treasurers' Association.
